Rounded to the nearest integer, what is the area of the parallelogram $ABCD?$
question.worked_solution:
The diagonal $\overset{―}{BD}$ divides the parallelogram into two congruent triangles. Therefore, the area of the parallelogram is twice the area of $△ABD$ (see the illustration).

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14226856/assets/7572dac85d8e6029b52d199bdfcb87b4a92ffafc008fe999c10848153f9f67d8.png)

 Computing the area of $△ABD,$ we find
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ABD} & =\frac{1}{2}(10)(6)\operatorname{sin}⁡{38}^{∘} \\  & =30\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{38}^{∘} \\  & ≈18.470,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places. Consequently,

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ABCD} & =2{A}_{ABD} \\  & =2\cdot 18.470 \\  & =36.940.\end{aligned}
$$

So, to the nearest integer, the area of the parallelogram is $37.$
